Every single person who waited made money.

posts.caption:
Every dot is one day of Bitcoin since August 2017. Gold means it closed at a brand new all-time high.

Only 3.2% of days were a record.
On 96.8% of days, Bitcoin was below its high.
On 39.2% of days, it was more than half off its high.

Over those same 9 years, $1 turned into $19.70.

If it feels like your coins are always down from the peak, they are. That's normal. Being below the high isn't losing.

posts.caption:
Every dot is one $5 coffee, every workday since 2000. 6,724 of them.

You spent $33,620 on coffee. Totally fine.

If each $5 had gone into the S&P 500 instead: $152,334 today.

The brightest dots are the coffees from the 2008 crash. The single best one was March 9, 2009, the bottom. That $5 is $56.79 today.

The money you were most scared to invest is the money that grew the most.

Keep the coffee. Just maybe not every one.

Price only, before dividends, not adjusted for inflation.

posts.caption:
Every card is an iPhone, one for every year since the first one in 2007.

Pretend that on every launch day, instead of buying the phone, you put $1,000 into Apple stock.

2007 iPhone: $76,559 today.
2008: $54,139.
2009: $66,987.

All 19 together: $19,000 in, $357,534 out.

I'm not saying don't buy the phone. I'm saying the company that sold it to you did better than the phone did.

Split-adjusted Apple stock, dividends not included.
